page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-dense virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 32 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio suited for memory-intensive configurations. The server does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached volumes for data persistence, and includes no discrete GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance testing reveals a divergence between general computing tasks and synthetic stress runs. In Geekbench, the instance delivers strong text processing results in the top 25 percent, alongside average multi-core and Clang compilation metrics. PassMark testing further demonstrates average CPU and database operation scores. In contrast, stress-ng multi-core and single-core benchmarks place in lower percentiles, while uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths measure 27.8 GB/sec and 19.94 GB/sec respectively. Static web serving throughput is limited, reaching 2.52 GB/sec, and inference performance remains practical primarily for small 135M language models rather than medium 7B models.

Because the server operates on a shared CPU allocation model, compute availability can vary under high-concurrency contention. The primary architectural benefit lies in its high memory density per compute thread, offering a cost-effective operational profile for tasks where RAM capacity is paramount but dedicated CPU threads are unnecessary. This balance makes the instance suitable for in-memory key-value caching, text analytics, batch ETL pipelines, and staging environments.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-32GB is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by 4 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz with x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It includes no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its text processing capabilities in the top tier, alongside average scores for Geekbench multi-core execution, PassMark CPU evaluation, and Clang compilation tasks. Conversely, stress-ng benchmarks and uncached large-block memory bandwidth reflect weaker throughput typical of shared CPU resource environments, and static web serving throughput is restrained. With its large memory allocation paired with shared compute, the instance provides cost-effective memory density for background data processing, intermediate caching tiers, ETL workers, and non-latency-critical memory-bound applications requiring substantial RAM without dedicated core reservation overhead.
